This diverges from the documented precedent and should be confirmed.
core/policy.ts (canApplyDiscount): unsure whether applying/removing a code should be gated by status (e.g. draft-only, like canEditLines). Would add a policy predicate if so; skipped it for now.

Whether code validation deserves a new core/discount.ts (a DiscountCode value object + eligibility rules) vs folding into rules.ts/policy.ts. I lean on folding to match the existing types/rules/policy split, but that assumes validation is server-side.
queries.ts: no change expected since totals are computed in core from the mapped Invoice — but if the applied discount must be re-fetched/validated on load, a query touch could be needed.
index.ts (public surface): I don't expect a new cross-slice export, since applying a discount is internal to billing's UI. Only touch it if another slice must read the discount.
questions: Is the code validated server-side (the apply mutation returns the updated invoice with the discount resolved) or client-side against a catalog the front-end holds? This decides how much lives in core vs data.
Is the discount a percentage or a fixed amount, and is it applied to the subtotal (pre-tax) or to the grand total (post-tax)? This drives the rules.ts math and rounding.
Which invoice statuses may receive a discount, and can a code be removed or replaced once applied (esp. on issued/paid invoices)?
One code per invoice, or should codes stack?
Do codes have lifecycle rules — expiry, per-client eligibility, usage limits — or is that out of scope for v1?
Should the invoice LIST read model (InvoiceSummary.totalMinor, used by the client overview) also reflect the discount, or only the detail view?
